speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Two-dimensional Schrödinger operators at one energy
summary: The talk moves from the failure of a naive all-energy analogy with one-dimensional inverse scattering to Manakov triples and the two-point Baker--Akhiezer construction. It explains potential and reality reductions by involutions of the spectral curve, Prym theta functions, and the two-dimensional analogue of KdV. The main constructions were published in 1976 and 1984. Several derivatives in the notebook are internally inconsistent; these are mathematical emendations of faithfully transcribed formulas. The final rapidly decaying assertion is less precise than the periodic construction. The actual heading is on P001245; P001244 still belongs to Feigin.

speaker: V. G. Knizhnik
title: Strings, moduli and quadratic differentials
summary: The second talk of 16 December constructs the critical bosonic-string measure in conformal gauge, explains the role of quadratic and Beltrami differentials, and works through the torus determinant before sketching higher-genus theta formulas. Novikov intervenes about the Schottky problem. The notes combine classical geometry, Polyakov\textquotesingle s 1981 formalism, and material soon published by Belavin and Knizhnik. They do not provide a rigorous measure on all embedded surfaces. The heading says \ru{Д. Книжник. (Дима)}; the catalogue identification as V.~G.~Knizhnik is retained with the discrepancy explicit.

title: The catalogue heading: Year 1986
summary: This is the catalogue heading \ru{Год 1986}, not a separate mathematical talk. The next supplied leaf begins Beilinson\textquotesingle s dated talk on 17 February 1986. No independent mathematical item is assigned to the heading, and its page reference denotes the boundary only. The academic-year item prefix remains 1985.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Quillen determinants, anomaly cancellation and the Mumford form
summary: Beilinson recasts the string determinant in the language of determinant lines and their Quillen metrics. A finite-dimensional comparison exposes a dual-line inconsistency in the written norm formula. The anomaly polynomial leads to the combination \(\lambda_2\lambda_1^{-13}\); Belavin intervenes with the holomorphic measure, low-genus theta formulas and divergences. The final uniqueness argument needs an overall normalization. P001258 and P001259 begin separately headed Kontsevich and Morozov talks (catalogue records 667 and 668), and are treated as adjacent evidence in a separate supplement, not assigned to Beilinson or counted as additional records in this chapter.
